title: Affineness of the norm nonvanishing locus
statement: Let s,t:R→V be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme], with s finite, flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let A be an affine open of V, W an open with s⁻¹(W) contained in t⁻¹(A), and f a section on A with D(f) contained in W. If an open U is contained in D(f) and its underlying set is W intersected with the complement of s(t⁻¹(V minus D(f))), then U is affine.

proof.text: Restrict s over W and pull f back along t into A. Finite flat locally finitely presented implies finite locally free. On local finite free charts take the determinant of multiplication by the pullback of f. Basis independence and compatibility with localization glue these determinants into a section g on W. Modulo the residue field its determinant is nonzero if and only if the fibre element is a unit, equivalently it lies in no maximal ideal of the finite-dimensional fibre algebra. The assumed set equality therefore identifies U with the nonvanishing locus of g. Restrict g to D(f), which lies in W: because U is contained in D(f), its nonvanishing locus stays U. Since D(f) is affine, its basic open U is affine. Empty fibres have determinant 1; no constant rank is used.
